docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This script uses the pyvisa library to communicate with external hardware over VISA protocol (e.g., GPIB, USB, RS232). It’s used to query device identity and test connectivity.

docs.title: setupDAQ.py
docs.text: This script sets up a Data Acquisition (DAQ) task using NI-DAQmx in Python. It defines which channels to use, the timing of the acquisition, and how the DAQ system starts and stops.

docs.title: Add a voltage input channel (AI0) to the task with a ±10V range.
docs.text: task.ai_channels.add_ai_voltage_chan("Dev1/ai0", min_val=-10.0, max_val=10.0) 2. Clock and Sampling Rate python Copy Edit

docs.title: Configure the task to continuously acquire samples at 1000 samples per
docs.text: second. task.timing.cfg_samp_clk_timing( rate=1000, sample_mode=nidaqmx.constants.AcquisitionType.CONTINUOUS ) 3. Start and Stop the Task python Copy Edit

task.stop() task.close() Output Summary The analog input channel is configured and ready.

Timing is locked in at 1 kHz continuous sampling.

The task is ready to be used in data acquisition loops or logging routines.

Why use this? This setup script gives you a consistent, reusable structure to:

Quickly initialize DAQ hardware

Avoid rewriting boilerplate setup code

Separate configuration logic from acquisition logic
